description: Runs the project's gdUnit4 suites in one engine and answers with every case that did not pass, with where it is and what its assertion said. The class list is rebuilt first, so a suite written a moment ago is found. What changed on disk since it was imported is then imported before any suite runs. On Windows and Linux the run gets a user:// of its own, away from a player's saves, which goes when the run ends, with every file a suite wrote there. On macOS the engine reads user:// off HOME, so it writes where the player keeps theirs. The run is headless unless a suite in it needs a window as gdharness test reads it, and then has one, on a desktop of its own on Windows. A run that found nothing to run is never called a pass, and names the path it looked in. A script that does not load stops gdUnit4 before any suite runs, and an autoload that does not compile stops the run at once. A client sending a progress token is told as each suite finishes, and at least every twenty seconds. A run whose every case passed is still not called passed when it printed a script error no case failed on. gdUnit4 fails a case only on the script errors its logger sees, and it cannot see a stack overflow. Needs gdUnit4 under addons/gdUnit4. The tool reference in the gdharness skill, and the site, say what every field of the answer means.

engineArgs.description: The engine's own flags for the run, such as ["--verbose"], a value going as the next entry. Only those that change what the engine logs, draws for debugging, checks on the GPU, which renderer draws, how it times frames or whether it builds the tree a screen reader reads: --verbose, --quiet, --debug-collisions, --debug-paths, --debug-navigation, --debug-avoidance, --debug-stringnames, --debug-canvas-item-redraw, --debug-mute-audio, --print-fps, --gpu-profile, --gpu-validation, --gpu-abort, --disable-vsync, --frame-delay, --time-scale, --fixed-fps, --max-fps, --resolution, --write-movie, --rendering-driver, --rendering-method, --accessibility. Any other is refused. With --verbose, engineEntries holds the ordinary lines the run printed as well, the newest of them, and a leak at exit is named in the note: the objects left alive counted by class, and the resources still in use, the project's own before its addons'.

failFast.description: Stop each suite at its first failing case. Default false: every case runs. With it on, the counts cover only what ran. notRun counts the cases left. Each run after a fix then finds the next failure. That comes from failFast, not a flaky suite.

ignore.description: Suites, cases or rows to leave out, as "suite_name", "suite_name:test_name", or "suite_name:test_name:N" for one row of a parameterised case, N being the zero-based index gdUnit4 reports the row under: a failure named "test_name:2 (3, 4)" is the third row, and the name can be passed back as reported. A bare test name is read as a suite name and leaves out nothing. An entry that named a case which ran all the same comes back under ignoreNotApplied with the form that would have left it out. Every case the list left out comes back under ignored as suite_name:test_name, and every row as suite_name:test_name:N, so a run called passed says what it did not run, and an entry naming no suite, case or row under path comes back under ignoreUnmatched.

path.description: A test directory or suite file inside the project, or a list of them, all run on one engine: a named set of suites boots once rather than once per suite. An entry given twice, or a suite inside a directory also listed, runs once. An entry "suite.gd:test_name" runs that case alone, as gdharness test reads it and as tests runs it, so it cannot share the list with a whole suite or a directory. An entry that is not there is left out and named under missing, the rest run, and such a run is never called passed. When no entry is there the run is refused before the engine starts, naming each one. A script named that declares no test_ function at the top level is refused the same way, and so is a directory holding no suite. A script that declares test_ functions and does not extend GdUnitTestSuite, which gdUnit4 never runs and never mentions, is refused when named, and under a directory run whole it is named under notSuites and the run is not called passed. A case declared there that gdUnit4 never ran, in a suite that passed, comes back under testsNotRun, a row it skipped for data that does not fit the case under rowsMismatched, and a case it skipped because it cannot run it as declared (a parameter nothing fills, or a fuzzer after a setting) under casesUnrunnable, each with the reason gdUnit4 gave. None of those runs is called passed. Default tests and test, those the project has, which is where gdharness test looks. With GDHARNESS_SUITE_FILES_ONLY set, a directory, the default included, is refused with the suite files under it, and only named suite files run.

printed.description: Also answer with every line the run printed that contains this, under printed, whether it passed or not: a suite that prints a marker beside the numbers it measured carries them back without failing an assertion to do it. Matched case aside, in the text and the backtrace, at most 200 lines, the newest kept. printedOmitted counts the rest.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the project directory, the one holding project.godot.

tests.description: Run only these cases of the suites under path, each "test_name" or "suite_name:test_name", the suite by its file name without .gd or its res:// path. Only the suites holding them run, with their other cases left out. A name no suite there declares as a top-level func is refused before the engine starts, with the nearest names, or the cases there when none is near. A case asked for that gdUnit4 did not report comes back under testsNotRun, and the run is not called passed.

timeoutMs.description: How long the run may take before it is killed, counted from the engine starting it: the class rebuild and any import before it are outside the limit, and tookMs counts them. Default 600000. A run killed at the limit answers timedOut and silentForMs, how long it had printed nothing. It is called hung only when that was half the limit, or thirty seconds of a longer one, and otherwise it was still running and wants a longer timeoutMs or a narrower path, unless it ended repeating one script error, which the verdict names instead. A run whose autoload did not compile is stopped as soon as the engine says so, and names the script that did not under scriptErrors.
